advisor.summary: In a 401(k) that covers employees, the ADP/ACP tests chain the owner's deferrals to staff participation — when the staff defers little, the owner's contributions come back as taxable corrective refunds. A safe harbor design buys the tests out: commit to a 3% nonelective contribution for every eligible employee, or to a matching formula costing at most 4% of participating pay, under §401(k)(12) (QACA auto-enrollment variants under §401(k)(13)), and the owner defers the full $24,500 for 2026 plus catch-up no matter what the staff does. The 3% nonelective also supplies most of the cross-testing gateway, which is why it anchors nearly every owner-max stacked design. This is an enabling strategy — the deduction it unlocks is modeled under the deferral and profit-sharing records, not here.
mechanics: The ADP and ACP tests of §§401(k)(3), 401(m) cap HCE deferral rates at a fixed spread over the NHCE average — with thin staff participation, an owner targeting a full deferral fails decisively and takes the excess back as taxable corrective refunds.

The §401(k)(12) buy-outs: a 3% nonelective contribution to every eligible employee whether or not they defer, or the basic match — 100% of the first 3% deferred plus 50% of the next 2%, costing at most 4% of pay and paid only to those who defer; the §401(k)(13) QACA variants pair automatic enrollment with a slightly cheaper formula and two-year vesting.
Safe harbor dollars vest immediately at 100% (QACA's two-year cliff excepted) — they leave with departing employees and never return as forfeitures.

The 3% nonelective typically covers most of the 5% cross-testing gateway, making it the default chassis whenever a new comparability or cash balance layer is contemplated; the match design contributes nothing toward the gateway.

Timing under SECURE Act §103: a match design needs its provisions and the participant notice in place before the plan year, but a 3% nonelective can be adopted retroactively until 30 days before plan year-end — or, at 4%, through the close of the following year — so a failed ADP year can literally be cured after the fact.

authority.note: The ADP and ACP nondiscrimination tests a safe harbor design buys out.
The traditional safe harbor formulas — 3% nonelective or the basic match — both immediately vested.
The QACA automatic-enrollment safe harbor: a reduced match formula with two-year vesting.
Eliminated the notice requirement for nonelective safe harbors and created the retroactive adoption windows — 3% until 30 days before year-end, 4% through the following year.
Sets the 2026 deferral limit ($24,500) and the catch-up amounts the design unlocks for the owner.

requirements: At least one non-owner employee in the plan — an owner-only plan has no ADP test, so safe harbor adds nothing there.
A funding commitment of 3% of all eligible compensation (nonelective) or up to 4% of participating payroll (match) for every year the design operates.
A plan amendment, plus — for match designs — the annual participant notice delivered before the plan year.
Payroll integration that calculates and deposits the safe harbor amounts accurately.
risks: The recurring compliance failure is timing and notice: a match design whose participant notice is late or missing loses safe harbor status for the year, reviving the very tests the client paid to escape.
Mid-year suspension of safe harbor contributions is permitted only in narrow circumstances and re-triggers full-year ADP testing — treat the funding as a firm annual commitment.

Picking the match to save money can foreclose the stack: the match never satisfies the cross-testing gateway, and owners who later add profit-sharing or cash balance layers usually regret not buying the 3% nonelective — design for the end state.
Immediate vesting means safe harbor dollars leave with short-tenure employees.
stateNotes: Employer safe harbor contributions are ordinary deductible compensation in every state that conforms to federal taxable income or federal AGI — the standard case; verify only in non-conformity outliers.
PTET interaction: the contribution reduces pass-through income before any PTET election is computed, so include it in the PTET estimate like any other deductible cost.
Missouri conforms through RSMo §143.121; for Missouri SALT Parity Act electors (RSMo §143.436), the safe harbor cost reduces the PTET base dollar for dollar.
reviewChecklist: Latest ADP/ACP test results pulled and the owner's current refund exposure quantified before recommending.
Formula selected against the end-state design — nonelective whenever profit-sharing or cash balance stacking is plausible — not merely current-year cost.
Amendment executed and, for match designs, the participant notice calendared and delivered ahead of the plan year.
SECURE Act §103 retroactive adoption windows reviewed when the year is already underway.
Owner deferral election raised to the maximum once testing relief is secured.

client.teaser: Shut off the IRS test that keeps sending your 401(k) money back.
client.headline: Save the full 401(k) limit — no matter what your team saves
plainEnglish: Many owners learn this rule the hard way. In a company 401(k), the IRS links what YOU can save to what your employees choose to save. If your team saves little, part of your own money comes back to you — with a tax bill.

The fix is a safe harbor design. Your business promises a modest, set contribution for employees — about 3 to 4 percent of pay. In return, the IRS turns the test off. You can save the full legal limit every year, no matter what anyone else does.
The employee money is not wasted. It is a real benefit your team can see. It is fully deductible. And it often becomes the base for larger owner-focused designs we may add later.
client.analogy: It is like paying a flat toll for the express lane all year. One small, known cost — and you never sit in traffic you cannot control.
benefits: Save the full 401(k) limit every year, with no test to fail
One small, known cost instead of surprise refunds at tax time
A visible benefit that helps you hire and keep good people
Lays the base for the bigger owner-focused plan designs
steps: WE pull your plan's test results and show what the cap costs you today.
WE pick the right version — flat contribution or match — based on where your plan is headed.
WE update the plan documents and handle the employee notice.
YOU raise your own savings to the full limit from then on.
clientCommitments: Fund the employee contribution every year the design runs
Send payroll data to the plan team on time
Tell us about big staffing changes so we can re-check the design

annualMaintenance: Deliver the annual participant notice (match designs) and verify funding
Reconcile year-end safe harbor deposits against payroll
Revisit the design when staffing or stacking plans change
deliverables: Plan amendment adopting the safe harbor provisions
Cost comparison memo: nonelective versus match, framed against the end-state design
Participant notice template and compliance calendar
